newsitem.title: FINLAND: Baltic Ice - Wind packs Gulf of Finland ice thicker.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Ice - Wind packs Gulf of Finland ice thicker.

text.p: Strong winds in the Gulf of Finland pressed eastern ice levels thicker while ice in the Gulf of Bothnia thickened slightly, the Finnish Institute of Marine Research said in its twice-weekly ice report on Thursday.
It announced no changes to restrictions to navigation, but one ice-breaker left Helsinki to assist ships outside Loviisa, Kotka and Hamina and one to assist ships outside Rauma.
Five other icebreakers were assisting near St Petersburg and Vyborg in the eastern Gulf of Finland, five in the northern end of the Gulf of Bothnia and two in the middle.
One ice-breaker remained on station outside Parnu in the
Gulf of Riga, the institute said.

NOTES: New ice - forming, thin and still moving. Fast ice -
not moving level flat ice. Level ice - thick flat ice.
Consolidated/compact - compact close ice. Windrow ice - reshaped
by wind, thickness varies sharply. Rafted - ridges forming,
10-20 cm thick. Ridged - ridged or hummocked ice. Open - floes
with water at rate of 4-6:10. Close ice - floes tightly packed.
